# Skein — full LLM context

Skein 0.5 is a tiny HTML-first Web Components runtime for interactive websites and documents. It adds fine-grained reactive state, keyed lists, conditions, component inputs and scoped lifecycle while leaving the rendering medium native: HTML stays HTML, CSS stays CSS, SVG stays SVG, Canvas stays Canvas, Web Audio stays Web Audio, and component boundaries stay Custom Elements.

Production entry: `skein.min.js`.
Current production size: 14,455 B raw, 5,267 B gzip, 4,753 B Brotli.
Runtime dependencies: zero.
Repository: https://github.com/Pom4H/web-component
Website: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/
Playground: https://pom4h.github.io/web-component/playground/

## Core philosophy

1. The browser is already the rendering engine. Do not introduce a virtual DOM.
2. Static content should remain static semantic HTML. Skein binds only dynamic data.
3. SEO-critical headings, links, product copy, article text, metadata and structured information should normally exist in the original HTML response.
4. Skein currently has no SSR or hydration. If request-time HTML is required, generate it outside Skein and enhance the result.
5. `{...}` contains property paths, not arbitrary JavaScript expressions.
6. Put derived logic in `computed()`.
7. Prefer native browser APIs over framework abstractions.
8. Component composition follows the platform: properties down, DOM events up.
9. Keep the runtime and official examples zero-dependency unless a task explicitly chooses otherwise.

## Smallest app

```html
<click-count></click-count>

<template skein="click-count">
  <script>
    this.count = 0
    this.up = () => this.count++
  </script>
  <button @click={up}>clicked {count}</button>
</template>

<script type="module"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Pom4H/web-component@main/skein.min.js">
</script>
```

No npm, CLI, bundler, config file or application server is required.

## External component convention

Custom-element names map to HTML files by replacing hyphens with slashes:

```text
<counter-app> -> counter/app.html
<user-card> -> user/card.html
<studio-mixer> -> studio/mixer.html
```

A component source can contain top-level `<script>`, markup and `<style>` in one file.

## State

Component scripts execute with `this` bound to a deep reactive Proxy:

```js
this.count = 0
this.count++
this.user = { name: 'Ada' }
this.user.name = 'Grace'
this.items = []
this.items.push({ id: 1, title: 'One' })
```

Synchronous writes settle in one scheduled microtask wave. There is no public `batch()` helper. Missing-property reads and array structure/length are reactive, including direct truncation.

## Bindings

```html
<h1>Hello {user.name}</h1>
<div title="User {user.name}"></div>
<input .value={user.name}>
<button ?disabled={saving}>Save</button>
<button @click={save}>Save</button>
```

Do not generate `onclick={save}`. The v0.5 event syntax is `@event={handler}`.

Context:

```html
<address in={user.address}>
  {city}, {street}
</address>
```

Context lookup is lexical and walks outward to root state. A present local property whose value is `undefined` still shadows an outer property.

## Component composition

Skein uses native Custom Element contracts instead of a separate framework component protocol.

Owner-to-child data uses DOM properties:

```html
<studio-mixer
  .wave={wave}
  .volume={volume}
  @mix-change={mix}>
</studio-mixer>
```

The child explicitly declares properties that should be reactive:

```html
<script>
  this.wave = input('wave', 'sawtooth')
  this.volume = input('volume', .18)
</script>
```

`input(name, fallback)` semantics:

- if the custom element already has an own property of `name` when its component script runs, return that value instead of the fallback;
- this preserves parent `.property={...}` writes that occur before an asynchronously loaded child component has mounted;
- install a host property getter/setter backed by the child reactive state;
- later `element[name] = value` assignments update child state reactively;
- repeated declaration during a Skein reload reuses the existing host accessor/state;
- the input is one-way with respect to the owner; changing child state or the child host property does not mutate owner state automatically.

Child-to-owner communication uses native events:

```js
host.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('mix-change', {
  detail: { name: 'volume', value: .3 },
  bubbles: true,
  composed: true
}))
```

The owner handles it with normal `@event={handler}` syntax. Use bubbling/composed events when the event must cross Shadow DOM boundaries.

Do not introduce provide/inject, a framework event bus or a store solely to connect Skein components. Shared application state can live in the owning component and flow to children as properties.

The reference composition is `examples/studio/`: `<studio-app>` loads and composes `<studio-transport>`, `<studio-sequencer>`, `<pocket-synth>`, `<studio-mixer>` and `<studio-scope>` as separate HTML files.

## Lists

```html
<article for={projects} key={id}>
  <b>{index}. {title}</b>
  <input placeholder="DOM state survives reorder">
</article>
```

Use stable unique keys when records have application identity. Without an explicit key, objects use object identity and primitive duplicates are disambiguated by occurrence.

List reconciliation is incremental: append creates new views, removal disposes removed views, reorder moves existing DOM nodes, browser-local form state can survive reorder, and `index` / `$index` are reactive locals.

## Conditions

```html
<section if={inspectorOpen}>...</section>
```

A conditional branch owns a child reactive scope. False disposes its effects, listeners, nested components and DOM view; true creates a fresh scoped view.

## Computed values

```html
<script>
  this.price = 100
  this.quantity = 2
  this.total = computed(() => this.price * this.quantity)
</script>
<strong>{total}</strong>
```

Computed values are lazy, cached and dependency-tracked.

## Effects

```js
effect(() => console.log(this.total))
```

Render work settles before user effects. If a user effect dirties rendering, render work runs again before later user effects.

## Component-script helpers

The injected helper surface is intentionally small:

- `input(name, fallback)` — declare a reactive host-property input.
- `computed(fn)` — lazy cached derived state.
- `effect(fn)` — user effect after render effects.
- `onCleanup(fn)` — deterministic cleanup owned by the current component scope.
- `host` — current Skein custom element; use for real host/shadow-root access and native events.
- `abortSignal` — scope-owned native AbortSignal.

Removed/not public: `batch`, `signal`, `untrack`.

Example cleanup:

```js
window.addEventListener('resize', this.measure, { signal: abortSignal })
fetch(url, { signal: abortSignal })
const frame = requestAnimationFrame(this.draw)
onCleanup(() => cancelAnimationFrame(frame))
```

The AbortController is lazily allocated only when `abortSignal` is referenced. Component input bookkeeping is also lazy and is allocated only if `input()` is used.

## Public module/global API

```js
Skein.version
Skein.define(tag, source)
```

`window.Skein` exposes the same object. Do not rely on runtime internals such as Scheduler, Signal, Effect, ReactiveState, `Skein.stats` or `Skein.flush`.

## Lifecycle

Every component owns a root scope. Lists and branches create child scopes. Disconnect pauses reactive effects; reconnect resumes dirty work without rebuilding. `connectedMoveCallback()` supports state-preserving moves.

Permanent teardown:

```js
host.dispose()
```

Renderer-owned list/branch removal disposes nested Skein custom elements automatically.

## Static HTML and SEO

Skein has no SSR today. This does not mean page content should be generated in JavaScript.

```html
<main>
  <h1>Creative websites with native HTML, CSS, SVG and Canvas.</h1>
  <p>Skein adds fine-grained reactive bindings without a virtual DOM.</p>
  <a href="/work/">See the work</a>
  <interactive-demo></interactive-demo>
</main>
```

If a server must compute personalized/request-dependent HTML, use an external server/static-generation layer.

## Native CSS / SVG / Canvas / Web Audio

CSS should handle layout, transitions and interpolation; bind state into normal properties/custom properties. Keep SVG as an SVG tree and update only dynamic attributes/properties. Canvas and Web Audio should retain imperative loops/graphs; use Skein for state, controls, composition and cleanup.

## Runtime architecture

Readable files:

```text
skein.js
runtime/reactive.js
runtime/template.js
runtime/component.js
```

`runtime/reactive.js` contains the dependency graph, computed values, scheduler, scopes, reactive Proxy and lexical lookup.

`runtime/template.js` compiles real DOM to compact instructions and implements exact DOM bindings, keyed reconciliation and branches. `.property={path}` writes the ordinary DOM property; it has no Skein-specific child channel.

`runtime/component.js` implements source loading/caching, Custom Element lifecycle, script execution and `input()` host-property adoption.

Important v0.5 implementation properties:

- binding paths compile once;
- ordinary lookup does not allocate frame arrays;
- list keys resolve directly against items;
- Scope resources, AbortController and component input metadata are lazy;
- declarative event cleanup does not allocate an AbortController per list item;
- production diagnostics counters are absent from hot paths;
- nested Skein elements are disposed with their owning view;
- disconnected instances are not permanently retained;
- an input can capture a host property written before asynchronous child source loading completes.

## Production build

```bash
node tools/build.mjs
node tools/build.mjs --check
```

The zero-dependency build concatenates readable runtime files, strips module-only syntax, lexically minifies and mangles known internal identifiers while preserving strings/regex literals. `skein.min.js` is tested directly in Chrome.

Current size:

```text
raw      14,455 B
gzip      5,267 B
brotli    4,753 B
```

## Testing

```bash
node test/run.mjs
```

Requirements: Node.js 22+ and Chrome/Chromium.

Coverage includes reactive core behavior, missing properties, arrays, exact bindings, keyed identity, nested disposal, lifecycle/reconnect, component input fallback and pre-mount property adoption, one-way property/event composition, the real multi-file Studio example, CSS/SVG/Canvas behavior, inline bootstrap, late registration, generated minified runtime correctness and Playground sandbox serialization.

## Current limitations

- no SSR or hydration;
- no built-in async resource/suspense primitive;
- no built-in error-boundary primitive;
- `{...}` expressions are property paths rather than arbitrary JavaScript;
- component scripts use `AsyncFunction`, so strict CSP currently requires `unsafe-eval`.

## Rules for AI agents

When building a Skein application:

1. Start with the smallest native HTML solution.
2. Keep semantic/SEO-critical static content outside client-only components when possible.
3. Use Skein only where state/interactivity is useful.
4. Prefer one-file `<template skein>` for tiny examples.
5. Use external tag-to-path component files when a project grows.
6. Keep `{...}` to paths and use `computed()` for derivation.
7. Use `.property`, `?boolean` and `@event` for native semantics.
8. For component composition, declare child host properties with `input()`, pass state down with `.property`, and send requests/notifications up with native CustomEvents.
9. Use stable keys for persistent list identity.
10. Use CSS, SVG, Canvas and Web Audio directly.
11. Register resource cleanup with `onCleanup()` or `abortSignal`.
12. Do not add dependencies unless explicitly requested.
13. Do not reintroduce removed low-level/public compatibility APIs without an explicit requirement.

When modifying the runtime, read `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/skein/references/architecture.md`, regenerate `skein.min.js`, and run the full suite.
